1.why: The system checks that the reset code belongs to the user by validating token.sessionId === session.id in /api/verify-token and /api/reset-password.

2.why: The same reset code cannot work for any other user because tokens are bound to sessionId and mockAccountHash, preventing reuse across sessions.

3.why: Previous sessions are invalidated after password reset (session.resetComplete = true), and old sessions are cleaned up via cleanExpired().

4.why: The website enforces HTTPS with TLS (Bun.serve with tls config) and redirects HTTP to HTTPS.

5.why: Reset codes are hashed with SHA-256 and stored with expiration/usage flags; user data is not exposed in plaintext.

6.why: Email messages (simulated logs) do not expose private user data; tokens are delivered via secure mock links.

7.why: User-supplied data (email, passwords) is validated via validIdentifier() and passwordPolicy(), and inputs are sanitized (textContent only).

8.why: Redirect links are hardcoded to the hospital’s site (e.g., /verify) and validated via allowedView() and urlForView().

9.why: Email templates (simulated) contain no user input; dynamic text uses textContent, not innerHTML.

10.why: Error pages/logs do not expose private info or tokens (generic messages like 'Invalid request' or 'Unable to complete').

11.why: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt (Bun.password.hash), and no secrets are hardcoded in the source.

12.why: No default credentials are present; all sessions/tokens require explicit generation and validation.

13.why: Rate limiting (consumeRateLimit, recordVerificationFailure) blocks excessive wrong attempts (e.g., 3 requests/10 min for recovery).

14.why: The system never reveals whether a username/email exists (generic response: 'If the details match an account...').

15.why: Reset codes are random (randomValue(32)), complex (base64url), and user-specific (bound to sessionId and mockAccountHash).
